sentences.text:
Sri Vasudeva Seshagiri, Hyderabad, And ... vs The State Of A.P.,
Rep. By P.P., ... on 26 July, 2024

The Honourable Sri Justice K.Surender
 Criminal Revision Case No.247 Of 2010
Order:

1. The 1st revision petitioner/A1 is the proprietor of the 2nd revision petitioner/A2 firm, who were convicted for the offence under Sections 16(1)(a)(ii) r/w section 7(i) and 2(ia)(f) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (for short "P.F.A Act'), by the trail Court and the same was confirmed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge in the appeal.
Aggrieved by the same, present revision is filed.
2. The Food Inspector-PW1 of Guntur District found 300 sealed water bottles (1 litre each) in the premises of the shop of A2.
The said water was meant for human consumption.
Suspecting that there was adulteration, PW1 purchased 9 bottles from the said stock and sent them to public analyst after following procedure for sampling.
3. The public analyst conducted test and the Report dated 06.11.2001-Ex.P14 was submitted.

4. According to the report, in the said samples, the total dissolved solids is 556.00 m.g. per litre and the permitted value as per clause A.33 in Appendix B to the P.F.A.Rules, should not more than 500.00 m.g. per litre.
All the remaining tests i.e. Alkalinity, Sulphates, Nitrates etc. were within the prescribed limits.
5. The permitted value of total dissolved solids is 500.00 m.g. per litre, however, 556.00 m.g. per litre was found, which is 56.00 m.g. above the permitted limit.
6. Since the adulteration margin is negligible, benefit of doubt is extended on the ground that there is a possibility of error in the analysis.
7. Keeping in view the negligible adulteration, this Court deems it appropriate to set aside the conviction.

8. Accordingly, Criminal Revision Case is allowed and the conviction recorded by the learned Magistrate in C.C.No.977 of 2006 (new), dt.25.03.2008 which was confirmed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge in C.A.No.52/2008, is set aside and both the revision petitioners/A1 and A2 are acquitted.
Since the 1st petitioner/A1 is on bail, his bail bonds shall stand discharged.
As a sequel, miscellaneous applications, if any, pending shall stand closed.
__ K.SURENDER, J Date: 26.07.2024 tk Sri Vasudeva Seshagiri, Hyderabad, And ... vs The State Of A.P., Rep. By P.P., ... on 26 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99792772/
